meta.provenance: Extracted from the Tradestands character record sheets (v6.0; Monk v6.3). Everything here is treated as an overlay on rules-core / rules-skills. Items marked 'unconfirmed' need you to say whether they are house rules.
meta.mergeOrder: Base rules (rules-core, rules-skills, gear) first, then this file overrides or adds. There is no core-rules-only mode: this file is always applied.

houseRules.description: The Monk is a 100% house class (confirmed by owner): its level table, abilities, XP, skills, prohibitions and prefills all come from house rules, none from the PHB/DMG.

INT 'Bonus Spells 1st-4th'. Wizard only (confirmed by owner, not the Bard). Uses the same bonus-spell table as WIS, looked up with the INT score. Shown on wizard sheets and multi-classes containing a wizard.
WIS field labelled 'Mental Save' on the sheets. PHB Table 5 calls the WIS value 'Magical Defense Adjustment'; the sheet label is probably the same value renamed. Confirm.
'Melee Move' movement rate shown alongside Normal, Encumbered and Swimming.
Equipment tracked in two lists: Melee Encumbrance and Normal Encumbrance, each with its own total.
Sheet rows for Raised from Dead, Hasted and Unnatural Ageing (20 boxes each). Probably tallies rather than per-level values.

Sheets print 'Non Proficient/Related Penalty' as two values (e.g. -3/-2 on the Monk). Non-proficient values come from PHB Table 34 (Warrior -2, Wizard -5, Priest -3, Rogue -3). Related-weapon penalty is half the normal amount rounded up (warrior -1, wizard -3, priest -2, rogue -2); see rules-skills.json proficiencies.weapon.relatedWeaponRule.
No class loses its Constitution hit point bonus after name level. ALL classes receive the relevant CON bonus at ALL levels.
Ignore all level limits by race and class: treat every level limit as unlimited.

To-hit numbers are calculated separately for each target AC from 10 to 0, using the character's BASE THAC0 for level and the weapon's armour adjustment for that AC (gear.json armourAdjustments, taken from the owner's weapons spreadsheet).
houseRules.formula: numberNeededToHit(AC) = baseTHAC0 - AC - armourAdjustment[AC] - strengthHitBonus - magicalPlus - specialisationBonus - racialBonus + nonProficiencyPenalty
houseRules.signConvention: The adjustment is subtracted. A negative table value therefore raises the number needed (harder to hit, e.g. -5 for a battle axe vs AC0); a positive value lowers it (easier, e.g. +2 vs AC10).
houseRules.oldMethod: Previously: THAC0 - STR bonus + weapon pluses + specialisation = final THAC0, then reduced by 1 for AC1, 2 for AC2 and so on.
houseRules.example: THAC0 20, battle axe, no bonuses: vs AC10 adjustment +2 gives 20 - 10 - 2 = 8; vs AC0 adjustment -5 gives 20 - 0 + 5 = 25.
houseRules.racialBonus: See rules-core.json races.weaponAttackBonuses (elves: bows, short and long swords; halflings: thrown weapons and slings).
houseRules.appliesTo: melee weapon armourAdjustments on the weapon (or its mode); missile and thrown weapons use armourAdjustments on the gear.json missileRanges row.
openQuestions: The spreadsheet has no column for AC below 0. How should AC -1 and lower be handled (e.g. reuse the AC0 adjustment)?
Should the DEX missile attack adjustment (PHB Table 2) also be subtracted for missile weapons, as in the standard rules? Assumed yes, 'as normal'.
Whether the non-proficiency penalty is added after the table adjustment (assumed).

sheetVariations: No Hit Prob / Dmg Adj on the STR row.
No Adjusted AC sub-lines (Surprised, Shieldless, Rear, Natural); the area has an area-effects note instead.
Thief skills subset: Move Silently, Find Traps, Climb Walls, Hide in Shadows, Hear Noise.
Extra damage with proficient weapons: 1 point per 2 levels.

stunAndFatalBlow.summary: With Open Hand a Monk may stun a humanoid opponent if the to-hit roll is exceeded by 5 or more, or a natural 20 is rolled (unless a 20 is required to hit). An opponent can only be affected once. Opponents are stunned for the remainder of that round and 1d4 additional rounds. Stunned victims suffer a loss of dexterity bonuses, -4 on AC, to hit and all saves, and are unable to cast spells.

stun.trigger: To-hit roll exceeded by 5 or more, or natural 20 (unless a 20 is needed to hit)
stun.affects: living humanoids and humanoid-shaped creatures (dwarves, elves, ogres, trolls, giants etc)
stun.noEffectOn: dragons, slimes, elementals, golems, creatures with three or more legs, undead etc
stun.duration: rest of the round plus 1d4 rounds
stun.penalties: lose dexterity bonuses, -4 AC, -4 to hit, no spells, -4 on all saves

dodgingMissiles.summary: Daggers, axes, arrows and crossbow bolts can be dodged or knocked aside; machine-launched missiles and thrown boulders can be dodged but not knocked aside. Saving throw vs Petrification (DEX bonus applies), -1 for each magical plus of the missile. One missile per level per round can be dodged. -1 Move per missile avoided, and the Monk cannot attack or activate any other special abilities. Magic Missiles or similar spells cannot be dodged.
dodgingMissiles.cannotDodge: Magic Missile or similar spells (Melf's acid arrow, minute meteors etc)

monkClassAbilities.prohibitions: Cannot use flaming oil or poisons. Cannot turn or command undead.

qigong.summary: The Monk's body counts as magical weapons for deciding which creatures may be hit (see the Qi column). This bonus does not apply to hit or damage rolls.
qigong.example: 13th level: body counts as a +3 magical weapon for deciding which creatures can be hit. Natural ability unaffected by magic or planes. Does not add to to-hit or damage.

monkClassAbilities.areaEffects: Against magical damaging spells or breath weapons where saving throws are allowed, the Monk sustains no damage if the save succeeds and only 50% of the total damage if it fails.

mindOverBody.summary: Suppress the need for food, water, rest or sleep for up to 2 consecutive days per level (10th level: 20 days). Also heals himself 2 hp per level once per day.
mindOverBody.recovery: Up to 48 hrs: no meditation needed, recharges after 48 hrs of normal rest. Over 48 hrs: meditation period equal to the total suppression time, with penalties (first 50%: 50% easier to surprise, -4 initiative, -4 to hit, half damage, -2 saves, half movement, no activated abilities; 51-75%: 25% easier to surprise, -2 initiative, -2 to hit, normal damage, -1 saves, 2/3 movement, activated abilities need a WIS check at -2; 76-90%: -1 initiative, -1 to hit, activated abilities need a WIS check; last 10%: normal). Activating abilities or fighting during meditation adds 1 day per day so spent.

mindMask.summary: ESP has only a 30% chance of success at 2nd level, dropping 2% per level thereafter. Permanent unless the Monk wills otherwise.

bodyControl.summary: Adapt to a hostile environment (water, acid, heat, cold, an elemental plane): breathe and move normally and take no damage simply from being there. Not a defence against attacks. Initiative modifier +3, lasts 1 hr/level, once per day.

immunities4.summary: Immune to all natural diseases (including those from magical items or spells; not lycanthropy or vampirism). Unaffected by Haste and Slow.

towerOfIronWill.summary: Resistant to charms, suggestions, hypnotism and mental attacks: 30% at 5th level, +5% per level thereafter. Permanent unless the Monk wills otherwise.

bodyEquilibrium.summary: Adjust weight to the surface (walk on water, quicksand); Feather Fall effect when falling. Once per day, 1 round/level, can change from round to round.

empathy.summary: Senses basic needs, drives and emotions of unshielded minds seen within range, in the facing direction, range 10 ft per level. Three times a day, 1 round/level.

youthfulness.summary: Ageing (natural and magical) slows to one third.

molecularManipulation.summary: Weakens a non-magical object not held by a creature (rope, leather straps, wooden boards, heavy chain, 1-inch iron bars) so it is easily broken by external force. Touch or sight within 20 ft, once per day.

immunities10.summary: Immune to paralysation and all poisons (including magical), and unaffected by Geas and Quest.

psychicImpression.summary: Once per day reads psychic impressions on an object. d20 against WIS modified by object type; the margin of success sets the knowledge gained (table below).
psychicImpression.artefactNote: Only one reading of a given artefact per level.

knowledgeByMarginPassed.1: Last owner race, sex and age
knowledgeByMarginPassed.3: Last owner general location (city or region)
knowledgeByMarginPassed.4: How last owner gained and lost item
knowledgeByMarginPassed.5: All previous owners race, sex and ages
knowledgeByMarginPassed.6: All previous owners names and alignments
knowledgeByMarginPassed.7: All previous owners current locations to town, city, region
knowledgeByMarginPassed.8: Complete history of how each owner gained and lost item
knowledgeByMarginPassed.9: Full details of who, where, when and how the item was created
knowledgeByMarginPassed.10: All details of any mundane item, and one detail of a magical item
knowledgeByMarginPassed.11: An additional detail/function of a magical item
knowledgeByMarginPassed.12: All details of miscellaneous magical items (command words, charges etc)
knowledgeByMarginPassed.13: All details of magical items +1/+2 and equivalent
knowledgeByMarginPassed.14: All details of miscellaneous special purpose magical items
knowledgeByMarginPassed.15: All details of miscellaneous magical items +3 or greater and equivalent
knowledgeByMarginPassed.16+: Everything there is to know about the item read including artefacts

quiveringPalm.summary: Once per week; the Monk must touch the victim within 1 round/level of generating it or it is lost for the week. Victim must have no more than 150% of the Monk's total hit points. The command to die must be given within 1 day per level, any time from the next round (initiative roll needed), at any range or plane. No effect on undead, creatures without a life force, other-plane creatures, or those he cannot touch. Masters of the Wind (12th) and above are immune. If the Monk dies first the vibrations fade.

dimensionWalk.summary: Moves through the dimensions: 7 leagues (21 miles) per turn walked, up to 1 turn per level in 24 hours. No normal encounters. Time may alter: d% 01-20 +10%, 21-75 0%, 76-90 -25%, 91-100 -50%.

trueSeeing.summary: As the 5th level priest spell True Seeing; once per day, 1 round/level. Initiative modifier 8; lost if damaged or disrupted.

mindBlank.summary: As the 8th level wizard spell Mind Blank; protects against devices and spells that detect, influence or read emotions or thoughts (augury, charm, ESP, scrying, wish-related methods etc). Initiative modifier 1; once per day, lasts 1 day. Permanent once gained unless willed off (off for 24 hours).

planeShift.summary: As the 5th level priest spell Plane Shift, affecting only the Monk. Initiative modifier 8; lost if damaged or disrupted.

wordOfRecall.summary: As the 6th level priest spell Word of Recall to his monastery; affects only the Monk and his immediate belongings. Initiative modifier 1.

astralSpell.summary: As the 7th level priest spell Astral Spell, only the Monk and his belongings. Initiative modifier 1 turn; once per day.

timeStop.summary: As the 9th level wizard spell Time Stop; initiative modifier 9; once per day.

levelTable.notes: Qi is the magical-weapon equivalence for deciding which creatures can be hit (shown as +N). dmgRange is as printed on the sheet. Note: level 5 qi printed '+1', level 19 printed 'Any'.

hitDice.rule: Levels 1-11: the Monk has (level + 1) d6 hit dice in total (2d6 at level 1, one more d6 each level, 12d6 at level 11). From level 12 he gains a flat amount of hit points per level instead of dice.
hitDice.conBonus: The CON bonus is added to the flat gain each level (house rule: CON bonus at all levels). Example: 12th level, CON +2: 2 + 2 = 4 hp. 19th level: 16 + CON bonus.
hitDice.note: The sheet's "12+2 ... 12+14, 12+30" column shows the running total; the real rule is +2 hp per level from 12th and +16 at 19th (owner clarification).

saves.note: Priest tables for all saving throws.

combat.proficientWeaponDamage: +1 hp per two levels attained when proficient (e.g. 10th level with a dagger: 1d4 + 5).
combat.noStrengthBonus: No STR bonus to hit or damage.
combat.noCriticalHits: Open Hand never makes critical hits (a 20 is just a hit); the Stun/Fatal Blow replaces critical hits.

allowedWeapons.note: Within the Forgotten Realms certain gods may allow other weapons. Mapping to weapon ids is in rules-core classes.byClass.monk.weaponRestrictions.
allowedWeapons.status: names only for now (owner: list at present); alkyls, atlatl, throwing stars and wakizashi have no weapon data
allowedWeapons.mappingConfirmed: Polearms = all polearms in the weapons table except the mancatcher; staff = quarterstaff (confirmed by owner)

rogueSkills.adjustments: Not adjusted for race, Dexterity or armour.
rogueSkills.note: Applies from level 1 (base score at 1st level, then 20 points to add at each level).

monk.ageing: Ages at one third the normal rate (Youthfulness, level 8; the docx also says 1 year of game time = 3 years real time for challenges).

orders.forgottenRealms: Monastic orders of various gods, each with its own hierarchy and patron god; several monks of the same level may exist in an area.
orders.masterRanks: Level 9+ (Masters/Mistresses) are strictly limited in number. To take a rank a monk must have the XP for the level and defeat the holder in unarmed combat (to the death or non-fatal depending on alignment). The loser (if he survives) drops one level to the challenger's level (XP midway between old and new level). A losing challenger loses half the XP needed for his current level and cannot challenge again until it is regained and at least 1 year has passed (3 years real time). Advancement without combat is possible when the post is vacant or the holder is an instructor.

druid.source: 2e PHB druid Granted Powers (text supplied by owner), paraphrased

grantedPowers.text: Saves as a priest, with a +2 bonus to all saving throws against fire or electrical attacks.
Speaks the secret druidic language in addition to any other tongues. Its vocabulary is limited to nature and natural events. Under the optional proficiency rules it does not use a proficiency slot.
Identifies plants, animals and pure water with perfect accuracy.
Passes through overgrown areas (thick thorn bushes, tangled vines, briar patches, etc.) without leaving a trail and at normal movement rate.

Can learn the languages of woodland creatures: one at 3rd level and one more for each level advanced above 3rd. Under the optional proficiency rules the druid chooses whether to spend a proficiency slot on these.
Immune to charm spells cast by woodland creatures (dryads, nixies, etc.).

Can shapechange into a reptile, bird or mammal up to three times per day; each of the three animal types can be used only once per day. Size ranges from a bullfrog or small bird up to a black bear. On assuming a new form the druid heals 10-60% (1d6 x 10%) of the damage he has suffered, rounding fractions down. Only normal, real-world animals in normal proportions, taking on all of the creature's characteristics (movement, abilities, AC, attacks, damage). Clothing and one item held in each hand become part of the new body and cannot be used until normal form resumes.

sheetOnlyAbilities.text: Can locate pure water within 1 mile + 1 mile per level above 3rd level (sheet wording ambiguous).
sheetOnlyAbilities.status: on your sheets, not in the PHB text supplied: house addition?

sheetOnlyAbilities.text: Can converse with all neutral/non-aligned woodland creatures.
sheetOnlyAbilities.status: on your sheets, not in the PHB text supplied: house addition?

paladin.source: 2e PHB paladin special benefits (text supplied by owner), paraphrased

specialAbilities.name: Detect evil
specialAbilities.text: Detects evil intent up to 60 feet away by concentrating on a direction. Can be used as often as desired, but each attempt takes one round. Detects evil monsters and characters.

specialAbilities.name: Immunity to disease
specialAbilities.text: Immune to all forms of disease. Cursed afflictions such as lycanthropy and mummy rot are not diseases.

specialAbilities.name: Lay on hands
specialAbilities.text: Heals by laying on hands, restoring 2 hit points per experience level, to himself or another. Once per day.

specialAbilities.name: Cure disease
specialAbilities.text: Cures diseases of all sorts (not cursed afflictions such as lycanthropy), once per week for each five levels of experience: once per week at levels 1-5, twice at 6-10, and so on.

specialAbilities.name: Aura of protection
specialAbilities.text: Surrounded by a 10-foot-radius aura of protection. Within it, all summoned and specifically evil creatures suffer a -1 penalty to their attack rolls regardless of whom they attack. Affected creatures can spot the aura's source easily, even if the paladin is disguised.

specialAbilities.name: Holy sword
specialAbilities.text: A paladin using a holy sword projects a circle of power 10 feet in diameter while it is unsheathed and held. This dispels hostile magic of a level up to the paladin's experience level. The DM explains the sword's other powers if one is acquired.

specialAbilities.name: Turn undead and fiends
specialAbilities.text: From 3rd level turns undead and fiends as a cleric two levels lower (at 3rd level, as a 1st-level cleric).

specialAbilities.name: War horse
specialAbilities.text: May call for a war horse at 4th level or any time after. The steed need not be a horse and is decided by the DM. The paladin does not simply summon it: he must find it in a memorable way, usually by a quest.

specialAbilities.name: Priest spells
specialAbilities.text: Can cast priest spells from 9th level, only from the combat, divination, healing and protective spheres, under the priest's spell rules. Spell progression and casting level are on Table 17. No extra spells for high Wisdom. Cannot cast from clerical or druidical scrolls, and cannot use priest items unless they are allowed to the warrior group.

magicalItems.note: Arrows and bolts are not counted toward the weapon limit.
magicalItems.sheetCrossCheck: The Paladin sheet has numbered Magical Items 1-10, matching the limit of 10.

wealth.text: A paladin never retains wealth. He may keep only enough to support himself modestly, pay his henchmen, men-at-arms and servitors a reasonable rate, and build or maintain a small castle or keep (funds may be set aside for this). All excess must be donated to the church or another worthy cause, and can never be given to another player character or an NPC controlled by a player.
wealth.appHint: Treasure block: warn when a paladin's treasure exceeds what he can keep, and do not allow transfers to other player characters.

tithe.text: Must tithe 10% of all income (coins, jewels, magical items, wages, rewards or taxes), paid immediately, to a charitable religious institution of lawful good alignment that he serves.
tithe.appHint: Offer a 'tithe due' calculator on income entries.

conduct.followers: A paladin does not attract followers at 9th level or on building a castle, but may hire soldiers and specialists, who must be lawful good in comportment.
conduct.henchmen: Employs only lawful good henchmen (or those who act that way when alignment is unknown). Cooperates with others of different alignment only while they behave, and will not abide those who commit evil or unrighteous acts. Non-evil thieves sincerely trying to reform can be tolerated. Stealth in a good cause is acceptable only as a last resort.

speciesEnemy.text: Species Enemy (+4 to hit / -4 reaction adjustment).

skillNotes: Hide in Shadows and Move Silently are halved if attempted in non-natural surroundings (e.g. crypt, city streets).
These skills are not possible in armour heavier than studded leather.
Wearing studded leather or lighter armour, a ranger can attack with two weapons with no penalty.

armourLimitForSkills.rule: Hide in Shadows and Move Silently are not possible in armour heavier than studded leather; two-weapon fighting without penalty needs studded leather or lighter.
armourLimitForSkills.byArmourClass: armour with AC lower than 7 is heavier than studded leather; ring mail (AC 7) also counts as heavier by owner ruling
armourLimitForSkills.source: Table 46 AC values (comparison by AC, as used for the bard); owner to confirm that AC is the right test for rangers.

ruling.text: Ring mail counts as heavier than studded leather.
ruling.why: Ring mail has the same AC as studded leather (7) but weighs more (30 lb against 25 lb), so a tie on AC is broken by treating ring mail as the heavier armour.

abilities.text: 5% chance per level to identify the general purpose and function of any magical item.

scrollUse.effectOnMisread: The scroll is read incorrectly and the spell's effect is reversed or goes wrong, almost always to the detriment of the thief and party. Exact effect decided by the DM.
scrollUse.sheetWording: Can read Priest scrolls at 10th Level - 25% chance failure
scrollUse.sheetWordingStatus: incomplete: should say magical and priest scrolls

classRecipes.description: Which blocks each class shows on a sheet. A multi-class character gets the union of its classes' blocks, one XP column and one HP-per-level row per class. Derived from the 20 provided sheets; they match this union rule.

bard.legacySheetNote: Old Bard sheet printed an INT Bonus Spells row; removed (INT bonus spells are Wizard only).

notes: Only the single-class Fighter sheet shows 'Specialized Weapons' and the point-blank (PB +2) range band; multi-class sheets with a fighter component omit both. Weapon specialisation is single-class Fighter only (confirmed by owner).
Paladin and Ranger sheets show no bonus-spell rows by design: they never gain bonus spells from WIS or INT (confirmed by owner).
Cleric/Ranger and Druid/Ranger sheets show the Ranger skills block next to the cleric/druid blocks; Cleric multi-classes add Turn Undead; Druid multi-classes add Granted Powers.
WIS bonus spells row appears on any sheet with a cleric or druid component; INT bonus spells row only where a wizard is a component (not the bard).

multiClassAlignmentOverrides.note: Confirmed by owner. The old Druid/Ranger sheet prefilled 'Neutral'; the new PDF should prefill Neutral Good.

labels.note: Corrected wording to use in the app and new PDFs, replacing sheet typos.

corrections.Hear Noise (Monk): Detect Noise (unify; keep 'Hear Noise' only if intended)
corrections.Find Traps (Monk): Find/Remove Traps (unify; keep 'Find Traps' only if intended)
corrections.Can read Priest scrolls at 10th Level -: Can use magical and priest scrolls at 10th level - 25% chance of misreading

wis.table: same bonus-spell table as INT (core WIS bonus spells, enter from PHB)

int.table: uses the WIS bonus-spell table, looked up with the INT score
int.note: Wizard only (confirmed by owner). The Bard sheet's INT bonus-spell row is not part of the rule and should not appear on the new Bard PDF.

bonusSpells.note: Paladins and Rangers never gain bonus spells from WIS or INT, so their sheets have no bonus-spell rows. A multi-class character gets a bonus-spell row for each casting class that qualifies.

conBonusAllLevels.overrides: The core rule that no class gains Constitution hit point bonuses after name level (9th for warriors, clerics and druids, 10th for mages).
conBonusAllLevels.meaning: Each class keeps using the CON hit point adjustment its normal rules give it: the +2 per die cap for non-warriors, and the warrior-only parenthetical bonus for fighters, paladins and rangers.

afterNameLevel.rule: After name level a character gains a flat number of hit points per level (3 for warriors, 2 for druids). The CON bonus is added to that gain once per level.
afterNameLevel.example: A 12th-level fighter with CON 17 (+3 for warriors) gains 3 + 3 = 6 hit points per level.

conBonusAllLevels.coreRuleReference: rules-core.json classes: hitPointsAfterNameLevel.conBonusApplies is the core value (false).

maxHitPointsPerClassLevel.rule: Divide each class's hit die by the number of classes to get the maximum hit points for each level gained in that class.
maxHitPointsPerClassLevel.userEntry: The user enters the hit points gained; the app does not roll. The app only checks that the number entered does not exceed the maximum.

rounding.rule: round UP to the next whole number (ceiling)
rounding.note: Owner example: 3.33 rounds to 4, so a Fighter in a three-class combination has a maximum of 4 per level; a d4 Mage in three classes has 2.

conBonus.perClassLevel: Each class's own CON hit point bonus (non-warriors capped at +2; the warrior-only parenthetical bonus for fighters, paladins and rangers), divided by the number of classes.
conBonus.sharing: Where possible the bonus is divided equally between the classes. Otherwise it is the user's option where they add it.
conBonus.appCheck: Simply check that the total bonus entered does not exceed the maximum: the sum over the class levels gained of (that class's CON bonus / number of classes).

example.text: A Cleric/Mage with CON 16 has +2 bonus hit points per level. At Cleric 5 / Mage 5, going to 5/6 gives the Mage level 1 point of the bonus. When the player reaches Cleric 6 he gets the other point.

conBonus.houseRuleLink: The CON bonus applies at all levels (house.json hitPointRules.conBonusAllLevels).

afterNameLevel.rule: The flat hit point gain after name level is NOT divided between classes. A class past its own name level gains its full flat amount (3 warrior, 2 cleric/druid/thief/bard, 1 mage) for each level gained in that class.
afterNameLevel.conBonus: The CON bonus still follows the multi-class sharing rule (class bonus / number of classes).
afterNameLevel.note: Applied per class: each class uses its own name level.

levelLimits.rule: No level limits by race or by class. Any race may advance in any class it can take without a level cap.
levelLimits.overrides: The core racial level limits (non-human races have maximum levels in each class).
levelLimits.scope: Level limits by race and by class, including every multi-class combination (confirmed). Which classes each race may take is separate and not yet supplied.
levelLimits.dataLimit: The XP tables stop at level 20 (Monk at 19) and the Turn Undead, saving throw and THAC0 tables run to 20 or beyond. That is a limit of the data supplied, not a game rule; the app's top level will follow the data unless you extend the tables.

multiClass.abilityMinimums: A character must meet the minimum abilities of each individual class in the combination.

startingFunds.status: applied in gear.json startingFunds.byGroup (owner dice, 10 gp x roll)
startingFunds.monkNote: Monks also keep no more than 25 gp per level (house rule above).
startingFunds.multiClass: see gear.json startingFunds.multiClass (average of the per-class rolls)
